zh: 窗口右移一格时，窗口和的变化只取决于新进入和刚离开的两个元素之差，这两个位置的下标对K同余。若能让每次变化在+1和−1之间交替，所有窗口和就只取两个相邻值。
按下标对K取余分成K组：余数为偶数的组从左到右依次放递增的小数，余数为奇数的组从左到右依次放递减的大数。这样同组相邻两项恰好相差+1或−1，又因K为偶数，相邻两次滑动的变化正负交替。
维护low=1、high=N；按余数r=0到K−1依次处理，组内下标r、r+K、r+2K……从左到右：r为偶数时填入low并让low加1，r为奇数时填入high并让high减1。每个位置只写一次，最后输出整个排列（任意合法排列都会被接受）。
en: When the window slides one step, its sum changes by the incoming element minus the outgoing one, and those two indices are congruent modulo K. If the change alternates between +1 and -1, every window sum takes one of two adjacent values.

Group the indices by their remainder modulo K: groups with an even remainder get increasing small numbers from left to right, groups with an odd remainder get decreasing large numbers from left to right. Then neighbours in a group differ by exactly +1 or -1, and since K is even, consecutive slides change the sum with alternating signs.

Keep low = 1 and high = N; handle the remainders r = 0..K-1 in order, and within a group visit the indices r, r+K, r+2K, ... from left to right: for even r write low and increase it, for odd r write high and decrease it. Every position is written once; print the whole permutation (any valid permutation is accepted).

explanationEn:
## Construction

Split the positions into K groups by index modulo K, numbered 0, 1, ..., K-1. Fill the even-numbered groups from left to right with the current smallest values 1, 2, ...; fill the odd-numbered groups from left to right with the current largest values N, N-1, .... Each step increments low or decrements high. When the traversal ends, every value in 1..N has been used exactly once.

## Proof of correctness

Any contiguous window of length K contains exactly one position of each residue class. Moving the window's left end from i to i+1 changes the window sum by `p[i+K]-p[i]`. The two positions belong to the same residue class, and adjacent elements of that group differ by exactly 1 in the constructed sequence: even groups increase, so the difference is +1; odd groups decrease, so the difference is -1. Because K is even, i and i+K have the same parity; as the left end moves right one step at a time, the residues of the positions it passes alternate in parity, so the change of the window sum alternates between +1 and -1. Therefore all window sums only alternate between two adjacent integers, and the difference between the maximum and the minimum is at most 1. When N=K there is only one window, and the condition holds trivially.

## Complexity

Each position is written exactly once: time O(N), space O(N) (for the output permutation).

## Verification

160 unique oracle inputs were checked against an independent permutation/sliding-window definition, and the construction was checked exhaustively for every 2<=N<=80 and every even K<=N, 1,600 cases in total. The 32 official test cases include the fixed OAMaster example and the boundary N=200000. Both wrong constructions are rejected by the semantic checker.

## Sources and site additions

The Amazon page for this problem gives the definition "among all contiguous windows of length K, the difference between the largest sum and the smallest sum is at most 1". [1Point3Acres](https://www.1point3acres.com/interview/problems/amazon-find-k-level-permutation) explicitly restates the same condition; the official Codeforces problem [1927E Klever Permutation](https://codeforces.com/contest/1927/problem/E) also gives the same definition and the even-K condition. The four window sums of the fixed OAMaster example `[1,7,3,5,2,6,4]` are [16, 17, 16, 17], with maximum 17 and minimum 16. This site adds the single-test standard input/output protocol and the bounds 2<=K<=N, K even, N<=200000; it does not claim these bounds come from OAMaster.
